priority_scale.name: Critical (Must have)
priority_scale.criteria: The system is not acceptable without it: explicitly marked high priority or mandatory in the sources, a hard technical/legal constraint, or demanded consistently by many stakeholders (e.g. a large share of survey respondents).

priority_scale.name: High (Should have)
priority_scale.criteria: Important for daily work of a significant user group and requested in more than one source, but a temporary workaround exists.

priority_scale.name: Medium (Could have)
priority_scale.criteria: Useful improvement requested by a single group or source; can be delivered in a later increment without blocking core use.

priority_scale.name: Low (Nice to have)
priority_scale.criteria: Convenience, cosmetic or speculative wish with weak evidence of need; candidate for future releases.

areas.name: Authentication & Staff Login
areas.description: Staff login mechanisms (username/password, card-swipe, optional streamlined login), session handling, login audit, and role-at-login behavior.

areas.name: Authorization, Permissions & Admin Scope Control
areas.description: Role-based and fine-grained access control for report and operational functions; admin capabilities for managing groups/roles, template edit restrictions, and scoped permissions.

areas.name: Web App UI, Help & Accessibility
areas.description: Web-based report writer interfaces, query UI/UX, interactive help (hierarchical/cross-linked/online), hover tooltips, and accessibility/non-interference with OPAC.

areas.name: Query Builder, Filters & Candidate Selection Engine
areas.description: Relational query capabilities for selecting/reporting entities: field selection, drag-and-drop, boolean logic (AND/OR), complex criteria, LIMIT/GROUP BY, regex/picklists upload files, null inclusion options, and displaying criteria/results.

areas.name: Report Templates, Scheduling, Queue & Outputs
areas.description: Canned and template-based report creation/management, run controls (ad hoc, modifiable vs run-as-is), scheduling/recurrence, queue visibility/status/cancel, report prioritization, pagination/progress, and output formats/exports (CSV/HTML/Excel/email).

areas.name: Analytical Reporting & Reporting Dimensions
areas.description: Core reporting analytics: grouping/aggregation levels, pivot/crosstab outputs, comparative date ranges and side-by-side views, trends, shelf-space proxy/reporting by category attributes, and demographic/inactivity/activity metrics.

areas.name: Location & Consortium Multi-Location Reporting
areas.description: Branch/system/region scope, cross-branch visibility, drill-downs, grouping branches by region/system, local-vs-system average comparisons, and centralized consolidation for multi-library operations.

areas.name: OP Operations: Item Transfer, Revert & Transit Management
areas.description: Batch transfer mechanisms and utilities (picklists/manual selection/query-driven candidate lists), audit/logging, preview/confirm, transaction safety, transit in-transit detection/thresholds/overdue rules, scheduled/conditional auto-revert, and undo for transfers including in-transit report variants.

areas.name: Purge/Weeding & Deletion Utilities
areas.description: Weeding/purge candidate identification with customizable criteria, read-only previews, safeguards to prevent accidental mass deletion, scheduling, deletions with DB triggers/audit persistence, reporting/audit trails, last-copy and WorldCat-support deletion lists, and orphaned record handling.

areas.name: Finance & Transaction Reporting (Fines/Payments/Accounting)
areas.description: Financial tracking and reporting: fines/charges by time/type, waived fines, snapshot/history, payments and instruments, ledger/audit trails, patron account balances, outstanding thresholds, and attachment/joining of financial transactions to records.

areas.name: Collections, Circulation & Capacity/Inventory Analytics
areas.description: Collection usage and volume analytics (acquisitions, circulation breakdowns, item counts by status/genre/format), item value and price/call-number aging, hold counts, uncataloged material tracking, and capacity/shelf-space utilization with color-coded status and central database aggregation.

areas.name: Patron Analytics & Demographic/Inactivity Reporting
areas.description: Patron demographics/behavior statistics, age calculation and configurable age ranges, last activity computation, inactivity thresholds, inclusion/exclusion of nulls/blanks, outstanding fines handling, inactivity/low-balance list generation, and completeness indicators for patron report outputs.

areas.name: Non-Functional Constraints & Platform/Deployment/Compliance
areas.description: Cross-cutting non-functional constraints and platform compatibility: relational backend and reporting replicas/warehouses, enterprise/centralized integration assumptions, performance under load & operational-hour processing, background processing/caching, scalability and large datasets, transaction safety/retention policies/anonymization, availability and cancellation behavior, OPAC isolation/non-interference, accessibility compliance and browser/server OS support.

glossary.definition: A library customer whose account, demographic information, holds, circulation activity, or financial activity may be represented in the system.
A staff member or other authorized worker permitted to log in, operate the system, or use reports according to assigned permissions.
An authorized staff user who runs, designs, schedules, reviews, or administers reports.
An organizational or physical library unit that owns, houses, or manages items and can be used as a reporting scope.
An administrative collection of one or more libraries that share operational data, policies, and reporting.
The broader group of participating library systems governed or operated together.
An owned or circulating physical or electronic copy that can have a location, status, circulation history, value, or transfer history.
The current physical or organizational location assigned to an item, which may differ from its owning library or transfer destination.
A recorded operational or financial occurrence such as a checkout, check-in, renewal, hold placement, payment, or registration.
A patron request for an item or title, including its placement method, status, fulfillment, and pickup state.
A set of selectable fields, filters, joins, grouping rules, and Boolean conditions used to retrieve or analyze records.
A generated presentation or export of queried, aggregated, or predefined system data.
A saved report definition containing fields, criteria, formatting, permissions, and optionally scheduling or delivery settings.
The software product specified by this document, distinct from the enterprise Library Automation System and from a library system or consortium.
Library material tracked for inventory or circulation without a complete bibliographic record.
The collection-management process of identifying items for review, withdrawal, discard, or purge; it does not itself imply deletion.
An authorized operation that permanently deletes selected records or related records from the system.
avoid: deletion when the broader audit or policy concept is intended

glossary.definition: A browser-based or Windows-compatible software interface used to access the reporting system; this term does not mean a library patron.

requirements.name: Staff Login Options
requirements.priority_rationale: The draft specification marks card-swipe and username/password login as high priority, and the agreed email discussion and later meeting minutes reiterate the need for card-swipe login while preserving optional use and a fallback.
requirements.description: The system shall support staff authentication using individual username and password credentials or card-swipe login, such as an RFID employee badge. Card-swipe login shall be optional and shall not require card-reader hardware; username and password login shall remain available as a fallback, including for staff without cards and branches without readers. A successful card swipe shall log the identified staff member in immediately. Streamlined login options shall be available to reduce login time and the security risks associated with password sharing and terminals left logged in compared with manual login.

requirements.name: Individual Login Accountability
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly describes individual identification as important for audit purposes and states that card-swipe login must not bypass individual authentication.
requirements.description: The system shall record which staff member is logged in whenever a login occurs, for audit purposes. Every login method, including card-swipe login, shall identify the individual staff member. Card-swipe login shall not bypass individual authentication or accountability.

requirements.name: Automatic Session Protection
requirements.priority_rationale: A frontline security problem is explicitly raised in one email thread, but no threshold or additional source establishes a higher priority.
requirements.description: The system shall provide automatic session protection to reduce the risk of terminals being left logged in and staff sharing passwords. This protection shall include mechanisms such as automatic session locking or logout. The source does not specify a timeout, so the system shall not assume a particular inactivity threshold from this requirement.

requirements.name: Password Change Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a single proposed missing report type in a reference document, with no higher-priority marker or evidence of broad stakeholder agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report listing staff accounts and the date of each account's last password change. The report shall allow IT and security personnel to review password-change dates across staff accounts. The source identifies this report as currently unavailable but provides no evidence that it blocks core login use.

requirements.name: Database Table And Field Permissions
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly marks control of table and field access as high priority, making it a stated security requirement.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to control staff access to database tables and fields used in queries. Administrators shall be able to restrict which data structures and fields each authorized user can access. This shall limit query access to the data appropriate for a user's responsibilities.

requirements.name: Fine-Grained Report Permissions
requirements.priority_rationale: Fine-grained report permissions are marked high priority, appear across several sources, and were prioritized by 76% of survey respondents.
requirements.description: The system shall provide fine-grained permissions that control which users can create, clone, modify, run, schedule, and view reports. Permissions shall be configurable for specific reports and shall also control who may add canned reports. These controls shall allow administrators to grant report capabilities according to users' roles and responsibilities.

requirements.name: Report Folder Run Permissions
requirements.priority_rationale: Shared-folder report permissions are marked high priority in the draft and repeated in agreed sources, including survey results.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to create shared folders for reports and assign permissions to specific staff for running reports stored in those folders. Administrators shall be able to allow or deny run access to particular reports through these folder permissions. This shall support controlled sharing of reports with the appropriate users.

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Control
requirements.priority_rationale: Role-based access control is explicitly marked high priority and essential, and is supported across multiple stakeholder sources.
requirements.description: The system shall control access to authorized system and report functions through configurable roles and security groups. Administrators shall be able to assign roles or groups to authorized staff users, and permissions shall be determined from those assignments at login regardless of login method. Permissions shall provide access appropriate to each authorized staff user's responsibilities.

requirements.name: Scoped Ad Hoc Dataset Access
requirements.priority_rationale: Control of ad hoc reporting on specific data sets is marked high priority, and a later agreed source also identifies shared folders as an access-control mechanism.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to allow or deny staff the ability to run ad hoc reports on specific sets of data. Administrators shall be able to use shared folders to control access to those data sets. These controls shall limit ad hoc reporting to staff authorized for the relevant data.

requirements.name: Template Edit Restrictions
requirements.priority_rationale: Template editing restrictions are marked high priority in the draft and reaffirmed in an agreed source; the sources identify dependable and accurate output as the purpose.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to restrict which template filters and display fields staff can alter. Restrictions shall be configurable to prevent front-line staff from changing a template to display deleted items. These controls shall help preserve dependable and accurate report output.

requirements.name: Predefined Role Capability Profiles
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed meeting provides a specific set of role access levels, and stakeholder sources also provide consistent administrative capabilities and concrete role examples.
requirements.description: The system shall support role profiles for Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and Patron. Global Admin shall have full system access, including software changes and configuration and statistical reporting for the entire system or consortium; Local Admin shall be able to configure local settings and run branch-level or system reports. Library Manager shall be able to run approved reports and make limited template modifications, while Staff shall run reports within assigned permissions and Patron access shall be indirect through OPAC displays. The system shall also support profiles such as front-desk staff with basic reports and limited filters, department heads with template creation and modification, and system administrators with full report and permission access.

requirements.name: Query Tool Access Control
requirements.priority_rationale: Administrator control of query-tool access was agreed and included in a consolidated summary, though it is supported by one source.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to control which users can access the query tool. Administrators shall be able to grant or deny access according to users' roles and responsibilities. This control shall prevent users from accessing query functionality unless authorized.

requirements.name: Role And Group Administration
requirements.priority_rationale: Multiple stakeholders and sources request role and group management and emphasize easy administration; role changes provide a practical way to manage permissions.
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to create, modify, and delete roles and security groups and to manage their membership. Administrators shall be able to change a user's permissions by changing the user's role assignment, with the user's permissions updated automatically to match that role. The system shall provide an easy-to-administer interface for managing report permissions and roles, avoiding the need to edit permissions individually for routine role changes.

requirements.name: Cross-Branch Capacity Access
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a specific operational need requested in one source, with no evidence of broader stakeholder agreement or an explicit high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall allow branch managers and other authorized roles to view capacity information for all branches, not only their own branch. Access to this information shall be governed by the user's permissions. This shall support operational decisions such as reallocating items or resources across branches.

requirements.name: Mass Deletion Safeguards
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed source identifies a consequential safety concern and proposes concrete safeguards, but the requirement appears in only one source.
requirements.description: The system shall provide safeguards against accidental mass deletion of collections. Safeguards shall include configurable limits or warnings for large batches, read-only previews, mandatory confirmations, role-based restrictions, and audit logging. These controls shall help administrators and technical staff prevent unintended loss of collection data.

requirements.name: Transfer Role Authorization
requirements.priority_rationale: A single source requests role-based limits on transfers; the need is concrete but has no explicit high-priority marker or broader evidence of agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall restrict the ability to initiate item transfers between branches to authorized roles. Authorized roles shall include managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators as configured by the organization. This shall prevent staff without an appropriate operational responsibility from initiating transfers.

requirements.name: Integrated Online Help
requirements.priority_rationale: C-145 is marked High Priority, C-497 identifies context-sensitive help as critical, and agreed requirements in C-530 and C-497 plus C-360, C-438, and C-145 show broad support across sources.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an online, HTML-based help system integrated with the reporting interface. Help shall be hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate, and shall describe and illustrate all system functions. The system shall provide context-sensitive help so users can understand the reporting functions relevant to their current task and reduce the need to contact IT for routine guidance.

requirements.name: Standards Compliant HTML
requirements.priority_rationale: C-154 is marked High Priority, C-449 calls accessibility non-negotiable, and agreed requirements in C-504 and C-537 specify standards validation across multiple sources.
requirements.description: The system shall produce valid, standards-compliant HTML for the web interface, online help, and report output. The HTML shall validate against applicable W3C standards. It shall use semantic structure and provide alt attributes and ARIA labels where appropriate, supporting accessible use of the web-based components.

requirements.name: Staff Report Authoring
requirements.priority_rationale: Custom report authoring is requested for staff in two candidates and supports a significant user group, though no source marks it mandatory or high priority.
requirements.description: The system shall provide library staff with a web-based report writer for creating custom reports. It shall allow staff to create and edit report content, recognizing staff as the primary report creators. This capability shall let staff develop reports through the web application rather than requiring a separate authoring interface.

requirements.name: Approved Report Type Coverage
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a proposed improvement from one source, with no priority marker or additional evidence establishing it as a core-use blocker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide every report type in the controlled report-gap register approved for the project. Before acceptance testing, the project shall identify the register by controlled artifact identifier and version and ensure it specifies each report type's required fields, filters, scope, and output rules. Acceptance testing shall verify each entry in that fixed baseline; report types not in the approved version are outside this requirement.

requirements.name: Large Location Usability
requirements.priority_rationale: One source identifies a concrete scale concern of 286 locations, but the request is a proposed consideration rather than an agreed or explicitly high-priority requirement.
requirements.description: The system shall remain usable when displaying hundreds of locations, including a set of approximately 286 locations. It shall provide mechanisms such as grouping or filtering, or other suitable interface techniques, to prevent the display from becoming overcrowded. These mechanisms shall help users work with location information at the stated scale.

requirements.name: Quick Access Descriptions
requirements.priority_rationale: The feature is identified as missing in one source, with no explicit priority marker or evidence of a workaround-free need.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a quick-access interface for users selecting reports and options. The interface shall display pop-up descriptions for reports and options to help users identify appropriate choices. This shall make common reporting choices easier to locate and understand.

requirements.name: Report Title Tooltips
requirements.priority_rationale: The same usability improvement appears in two sources, but neither supplies a high-priority marker or evidence that it blocks core reporting use.
requirements.description: The system shall display a brief description when an authorized staff user hovers over the title of a report template in the report-selection interface. The description shall identify the template's purpose before the staff user selects it. Acceptance testing shall verify that a configured description appears for each template with a description and that templates without one do not display misleading text.

requirements.name: Usable Reports Interface
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is grounded in a staff survey but appears in only one candidate and has no reported survey percentage or explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an intuitive reports interface that helps staff find and run the reports they need. The interface shall make report choices and the steps to run a selected report understandable to users. This shall address reported difficulty locating needed reports and support staff in completing routine reporting tasks.

requirements.name: Combine Query Criteria
requirements.priority_rationale: Boolean operators are explicitly marked high priority and are requested in several sources, including an agreed multi-participant request; customizable status, time, and activity criteria are also agreed.
requirements.description: The system shall let report users combine query clauses using AND and OR Boolean operators and group clauses. Supported item statuses shall include missing, discard or weed, and damaged, as defined by the Library Automation System status codes. A time-in-status criterion shall mean elapsed time since the item entered its current status, and activity criteria shall include elapsed time since last circulation. Acceptance testing shall verify combined criteria against records with known statuses, status-entry dates, and circulation dates.

requirements.name: Display Query Criteria
requirements.priority_rationale: Displaying criteria with results is marked high priority in a draft specification and appears again in an agreed request.
requirements.description: The system shall display the query selection criteria alongside the resulting records. The displayed criteria shall clearly identify the selections used to generate the report. This shall allow staff and auditors to understand how the result set was produced.

requirements.name: Include Null And Blank Values
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is stated as a must in agreed meeting notes and is repeated across a draft specification, reference document, and survey; a later agreed decision supersedes the earlier question about whether users should choose to exclude nulls.
requirements.description: The system shall include records with null or blank field values in query and report results rather than implicitly filtering them out. This behavior shall apply regardless of the selected filters or displayed fields. This shall make records with missing data visible in reporting.

requirements.name: Select Picklist Values
requirements.priority_rationale: Picklist selection is explicitly marked high priority in a draft specification and is also included in an agreed request.
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to select query values from picklists of possible values. Picklist selection shall be available while designing a query. This shall help users supply valid filter values without having to enter them manually.

requirements.name: Select Report Fields
requirements.priority_rationale: Field selection is explicitly marked high priority in a draft specification, appears in an agreed request, and limited field availability is identified as a current limitation.
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to choose fields to query and fields to display in a report. Report authors shall be able to select fields using drag-and-drop. The system shall expose a comprehensive set of database fields rather than a limited subset so users can build reports with the data they need.

requirements.name: Usable Query Designer
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is explicitly marked high priority in a draft specification and is also included in an agreed request from library staff and directors.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an interface that allows authorized staff users to design queries across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records without requiring specialist technical skills. The interface shall expose the supported fields and query criteria and provide validation feedback for incomplete or invalid criteria. Acceptance testing shall verify that a staff user can create and run a query for each supported record type using the displayed controls.

requirements.name: Use Regular Expressions
requirements.priority_rationale: Regular-expression support is explicitly marked high priority in a draft specification, identified as a current limitation, and included in an agreed request.
requirements.description: The system shall support regular-expression matching in query and report filters. Staff shall be able to select regular expressions from a dropdown when designing queries. This shall enable advanced matching while making available expressions discoverable to users.

requirements.name: Complete Data Specifications
requirements.priority_rationale: Complete data specifications are agreed and described as essential, with the requirement repeated in meeting minutes and later meeting notes.
requirements.description: The system developer shall provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold, and other records maintained or accessed by the system. The specifications shall identify record and field names, data types, relationships, and which records and fields are available for querying. The documentation shall be delivered with the system and reviewed against the data structures available to report authors, developers, integrators, and data architects.

requirements.name: Filter And Sort Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: Basic filtering and sorting are identified as needed, and a survey reports that some relevant fields are not currently available for filtering.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report authors and users to filter and sort report definitions and results. Filtering shall be available on relevant report fields, including fields that are not currently filterable. This shall let users create and refine reports using the data they need.

requirements.name: Filter By Survey Name
requirements.priority_rationale: The same need appears in a draft specification and meeting notes, with the latter defining the required name-to-ID resolution.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter reports by survey name rather than requiring them to enter a survey ID. The system shall resolve the selected survey name to its corresponding ID internally. This shall make survey-based filtering usable without requiring users to know internal identifiers.

requirements.name: Group Patron Results
requirements.priority_rationale: The request is agreed and described as essential for program planning by a stakeholder, but comes from one source.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to group report results by patron age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. Grouping shall support aggregates such as checkout counts by age range. This shall help staff analyze patron activity for planning purposes.

requirements.name: Identify Data Quality Issues
requirements.priority_rationale: Specific data-quality report needs are identified in a reference document and emphasized in a stakeholder interview.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports that identify bibliographic records missing specified MARC fields. It shall also report items with invalid item types, items with excessively long call numbers, and bibliographic records with no item records. This shall help cataloging staff find records that need data-quality review.

requirements.name: Identify Purge Candidates
requirements.priority_rationale: Cataloging staff agreed on customizable purge criteria, and the source provides concrete status, time, and activity examples.
requirements.description: The system shall allow cataloging staff to identify item records for purging using customizable criteria. Criteria shall include item status, such as missing or discard/weed, time spent in a status, and activity such as time since last circulation. Users shall be able to combine applicable criteria to identify the items that meet their purge policy.

requirements.name: Normalized, Isolated Reporting Architecture
requirements.priority_rationale: Reporting isolation and historical-data handling are requested across multiple sources, and database impact is identified as a significant concern; a normalized architecture provides a clear, consistent constraint.
requirements.description: The system shall support reporting queries over normalized relational data and shall not require a denormalized copy of production data. Reporting workloads shall be isolated from production transactions using a read-only replica, normalized historical store, snapshots, or an equivalent architecture; reporting access shall not modify source records. The implementation shall document data synchronization and reconciliation, workload isolation, and the data-through timestamp, which each report shall identify. Denormalized reporting stores are not permitted by this requirement.

requirements.name: Present MARC Fields Per Record
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is repeated in a draft specification and a survey, with the survey identifying a concrete problem affecting cataloging and reporting staff.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to select and extract specific MARC fields for reports. It shall present the selected MARC fields for each bibliographic record on a single row rather than spreading that record's fields across multiple rows. This shall make the extracted fields usable together in report results.

requirements.name: Query Across Record Types
requirements.priority_rationale: Access to all record types and the named open-template attributes are requested in multiple candidates, including an agreed request.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to design and run queries against all record types available to the system. Open report templates shall expose attributes associated with circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records for both filtering and display. This shall allow staff to build queries across the record domains needed for reporting.

requirements.name: Select Records From Query Results
requirements.priority_rationale: Manual selection is requested in an email, a stakeholder interview, and survey results, where 39% requested the capability.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized staff users to select individual records or items from query results for a targeted action. The selection shall be limited to the results the staff user chooses, rather than automatically including the complete query result. Transfer workflows and other supported targeted actions shall use this reusable selection capability.

requirements.name: Transfer Candidate Query and Preparation
requirements.priority_rationale: Candidate-material queries appear in a stakeholder interview and a survey, with 44% of respondents requesting the capability; a separate request also describes a concrete location and inactivity use case.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a query capability for identifying candidate items for transfer, including criteria such as item location and circulation inactivity. Authorized staff users shall be able to review the query results and prepare a transfer batch from selected candidates; selection of individual results shall use the reusable result-selection capability in REQ-DATAQ-017. This shall combine query-driven discovery with controlled preparation of transfer batches.

requirements.name: Upload Identifier Filters
requirements.priority_rationale: Identifier-file filtering is requested in a draft specification and listed as a missing feature in a reference document.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to upload a text file of identifiers and use those identifiers as report filter criteria. Supported examples shall include barcodes and TCNs. This shall let users select report records by supplying a prepared identifier list.

requirements.name: Filter Transaction Details
requirements.priority_rationale: The specific transaction filters are requested in one draft specification, with no additional priority or agreement evidence.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter reports by transaction date and time, workstation, and staff member. Users shall be able to apply these criteria when running a report. This shall support investigation and reporting of transactions by when, where, and by whom they occurred.

requirements.name: Reuse Existing Query Tool
requirements.priority_rationale: Reuse or integration is proposed by technical staff in one source, with no evidence that it is mandatory or agreed.
requirements.description: The system shall support reuse or integration of the existing report query tool for candidate selection. This shall allow staff to use established query capabilities when identifying candidate records. The implementation shall preserve the ability to apply the candidate-selection queries required by the system.

requirements.name: Board and External Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: A source marks board and external reports high priority, and the reports include statistics tied to formal state reporting; multiple sources request predefined board or executive reports.
requirements.description: The system shall provide the predefined reports for library boards and external reporting needs, including the Georgia Annual Report and the Application for State Aid. Before acceptance testing, the project shall identify the controlled, approved, versioned report catalog and applicable form versions, including required fields, calculations, reporting periods, and output rules. Acceptance testing shall verify each report against that fixed baseline; changes require an approved version update.

requirements.name: Create, Edit, and Version Report Templates
requirements.priority_rationale: Template creation is marked high priority in one source, has 81% survey support, and is requested across multiple sources.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report administrators to create report templates, edit their saved configuration, and maintain versions when a template is changed. Report administrators shall be able to make templates available to report users subject to assigned permissions. This requirement covers the saved template lifecycle; cloning is covered by REQ-RPTMG-026, and run-specific changes are covered by REQ-RPTMG-006.

requirements.name: Report and Capacity Data Export Formats
requirements.priority_rationale: CSV, Excel, and HTML are explicitly described as required, and survey support for multiple formats is 61%; several sources request the capability.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to export report outputs and capacity data in CSV, Excel, and HTML formats. Capacity data, including capacity views, shall be exportable in CSV or Excel for use in spreadsheet applications. Report users shall be able to select an available format appropriate to their intended use.

requirements.name: Report Job Prioritization
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed source calls prioritization crucial, and multiple sources request the ability to move important reports ahead in the queue.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized administrators to prioritize specific report jobs or report types in the processing queue. Prioritized reports shall move ahead of other queued reports, including resource-consuming ad hoc queries, so that important reports such as a director's board report can run sooner. The system shall display report priority and provide controls for changing it.

requirements.name: Report Queue Visibility
requirements.priority_rationale: Queue visibility is requested across multiple sources, is marked high priority in one source, and received 68% survey support; status information is also reported to reduce help-desk calls.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to see their submitted report's position in the processing queue and how many reports are ahead of it. The system shall display report status as waiting, running, completed, or failed, together with the report submission timestamp. This shall help users understand progress and reduce requests to IT for status information.

requirements.name: Run Report Templates With Optional Run-Time Changes
requirements.priority_rationale: C-193 explicitly marks this capability as high priority, and C-305 separately agrees that templates should be runnable as-is.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to run a report template as saved or change supported criteria for an individual run without changing the saved template. Access to templates and run-time changes shall follow assigned permissions. This requirement covers execution and run-specific changes; saved template creation, editing, and versioning are covered by REQ-RPTMG-002, and cloning is covered by REQ-RPTMG-026.

requirements.name: Versioned Report Definition Catalog
requirements.priority_rationale: The draft specification marks this item high priority and states that the system must support the Appendix A definitions.
requirements.description: The system shall support the report definitions in a controlled, versioned report catalog that identifies each report, its fields, filters, scope, and output rules, including the definitions formerly referenced as Appendix A and Appendix B. Before acceptance testing, the project shall include the catalog's controlled artifact identifier and approved version in the specification. Acceptance testing shall verify every definition in that fixed version; changes to the catalog require an approved version update.

requirements.name: Canned Report Display Editing
requirements.priority_rationale: Two sources request editable canned-report displays, including field selection and column presentation options.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to edit display options for canned reports. Users shall be able to add or remove displayed fields, such as shelving location, and change the order and format of displayed columns. This shall allow report authors and administrators to tailor report presentation to users' needs.

requirements.name: Circulation Report Catalog
requirements.priority_rationale: Circulation reporting is detailed in the draft specification and was selected by 78% of survey respondents as a standard report type.
requirements.description: The system shall provide circulation reports for check-ins, check-outs, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, total circulation, and items overdue by a specified number of days. Reports shall support breakdowns by circulation modifier, Cat1, Cat2, Dewey, shelving location, MARC, and circulation location. Circulation-location reports shall support breakdowns by patron county and home library, and reports shall also support age-demographic breakdowns.

requirements.name: Custom Local Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The survey indicates that 38% use custom reports and provides several concrete report examples, showing a meaningful user need.
requirements.description: The system shall support the creation and use of custom or local reports. Supported examples shall include collection development reports, program attendance tracking, and staff productivity reports, including time spent per transaction. This shall enable local library staff to report on needs beyond predefined report definitions.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.priority_rationale: Email delivery is requested in two sources and received 45% support in the survey, indicating meaningful but not majority demand.
requirements.description: The system shall deliver generated reports by email to one or more recipients entered by a report user or selected from an address book. Before delivery, the report user shall be able to review and change the recipient list. The system shall report whether delivery succeeded or failed for each recipient so report users can verify the delivery outcome.

requirements.name: Holds Report Catalog
requirements.priority_rationale: The holds report set is detailed in one draft source, and a separate source specifically identifies the Holds Purchase Alert as missing.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for Holds Purchase Alerts, items sent for holds, items received for holds, unfilled holds, annual hold counts, and stale holds awaiting pickup. It shall provide IntraPINES loan reports for the consortium and library systems, with results broken down by those scopes. Each report shall identify its reporting scope and period so authorized staff users can interpret results consistently.

requirements.name: PINES Library Templates
requirements.priority_rationale: Two meeting sources affirm the need for templates across PINES libraries, including a unanimously carried motion.
requirements.description: The system shall support identifying, creating, and delivering the report templates needed by PINES libraries. The templates shall be available for use across those libraries. This shall address the template needs agreed for the PINES library community.

requirements.name: Recurring Report Scheduling
requirements.priority_rationale: The survey reports that 52% prioritized the ability to schedule recurring reports, indicating substantial user demand.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to schedule reports to run on a recurring basis. Report schedulers shall be able to use this capability for reports that need to run repeatedly. This shall reduce the need to initiate each recurring report manually.

requirements.name: Report Cancellation
requirements.priority_rationale: Four sources request cancellation of scheduled or running reports, and a meeting source confirms the required cancellation checks are technically feasible.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users or administrators to cancel a scheduled report or a report that is currently running. During processing, the system shall check for cancellation signals and stop the report when cancellation is requested. This shall give users control over unwanted or no-longer-needed report jobs.

requirements.name: Report Criteria Display
requirements.priority_rationale: Two sources request showing criteria with results, including the date selection and report name.
requirements.description: The system shall display the selection criteria used to generate a report alongside its results. The displayed information shall include the selected date criteria and the report name, positioned at the top or bottom of the results. This shall help report consumers understand the scope and origin of the results.

requirements.name: Reporting Interface Options
requirements.priority_rationale: The draft specification says all three interfaces are needed, but provides no explicit high-priority marker or evidence from additional sources.
requirements.description: The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: predefined report templates, on-demand reports configured for a specific run, and open-template reporting. The interface shall identify the selected mode and provide the controls needed to run or configure it; open-template reporting shall support ad hoc reporting by advanced report users. Acceptance testing shall verify that a report user can run a predefined template, change run-time criteria for an on-demand report, and create or configure an open template.

requirements.name: Save and Reuse Queries and Report Templates
requirements.priority_rationale: C-058 describes repeated monthly use as crucial, while C-383 and C-061 also request saving, reuse, or sharing.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to save queries and report templates for repeated use, including recurring monthly work. Report users shall be able to share saved queries or templates with other authorized staff users when permitted by assigned roles. Changes shall be governed by the applicable template permissions; conversion between saved queries and report templates and version history are not required by this capability.

requirements.name: Scheduled Report Frequencies
requirements.priority_rationale: Scheduling options are requested in more than one source, and one source lists the full set of required frequencies.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to run a report as soon as possible or schedule it to run hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. The selected frequency shall be available when configuring the report schedule, and hourly scheduling shall be supported alongside the other listed frequencies.

requirements.name: Standard Report Categories
requirements.priority_rationale: A survey identifies broad staff demand, including 78% for circulation, 65% for item, and 52% for patron reports.
requirements.description: The system shall provide standard report categories for circulation, items, patrons, finances, and holds, as well as custom and on-demand reports. Examples shall include circulation check-outs, check-ins, and renewals; item inventory, weeding, and missing-item reports; patron demographics and inactive accounts; and fines and payments. This shall give library staff access to commonly requested report types.

requirements.name: Template Run Modification
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement was agreed by staff and administrators, with consistency identified as the reason for preserving the original template.
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to modify a report template for an individual run without changing the original template. Run-specific modifications shall not compromise the original template or its results. This shall let staff adapt a report while preserving a consistent reusable template.

requirements.name: Batch Report Execution
requirements.priority_rationale: Requested in two sources as a useful capability, with no high-priority marker or evidence that it blocks core use.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to select multiple saved or canned reports and run them in one operation. When requested, the system shall present the results together in a single document. This shall reduce the effort of running and reviewing related reports individually.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Record Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The report set is specified in one draft source without an explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide bibliographic record reports for total records, edited records, and records added by user and library. It shall also provide reports for bibliographic records with no attached volumes and records missing specified MARC fields. These reports shall help staff identify and review bibliographic record counts and data issues.

requirements.name: Check-In Type Counts
requirements.priority_rationale: Requested in one draft specification, with no evidence of a blocking need or high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide individual and cumulative check-in counts by check-in type. Supported types shall include book-drop, terminal, user, and self-service check-ins. This shall allow staff to review check-in activity by its method or source.

requirements.name: Check-Out Type Counts
requirements.priority_rationale: Requested in one draft specification, with no evidence of a blocking need or high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide individual and cumulative counts for staff check-outs, self check-outs, staff renewals, self check-out renewals, online renewals, and OPAC renewals. Staff shall be able to review activity separately by these transaction types. This shall support analysis of circulation activity across service methods.

requirements.name: Clone Report Templates
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed email source identifies cloning as a distinct useful capability, but there is no evidence it is essential to core use.
requirements.description: The system shall allow a report user with the required permission to clone an existing report template and save the clone as a separate template for further modification. Cloning shall not alter the original template. This requirement covers creation of a new template from an existing one; editing and versioning the saved template are covered by REQ-RPTMG-002, and run-specific changes are covered by REQ-RPTMG-006.

requirements.name: Excel Export Deduplication
requirements.priority_rationale: A single survey response identifies duplicate rows as a problem, with no broader priority evidence.
requirements.description: The system shall provide Excel exports without excessive duplicate rows or provide an option to deduplicate exported rows. Users shall be able to obtain a spreadsheet with redundant rows removed when needed. This shall address the stated difficulty of using exported data in Excel.

requirements.name: Executive Report Interface
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed meeting source identifies the interface and report list as a relevant need, but does not specify high-priority functionality.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an Executive Reports Interface containing a compiled list of reports needed for executive use. The interface shall make those reports accessible to executive stakeholders. This shall support executive access to the reports identified for their use.

requirements.name: Hold Type Subtotals
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft specification requests these specific subtotals, with no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall subtotal holds by hold type in reports. Supported types shall include active, frozen, and frozen-until holds. This shall allow staff to review hold totals separately by type.

requirements.name: In-House Use Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft specification requests these reports and provides no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts. Staff shall be able to review these in-house use measures in report form. This shall support analysis of library materials used on site.

requirements.name: On-Demand Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: On-demand reporting is described in a draft source and is included as a standard report category in survey results, but survey support for custom/on-demand reports is 29%.
requirements.description: The system shall provide preset reports that users can run on demand for maintenance reporting and collections development. These reports shall use preselected criteria to support repeatable report runs. This shall let staff request relevant reports when needed rather than waiting for a scheduled run.

requirements.name: Periodic Operational Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The cited evidence is primarily a single draft request and does not establish a mandatory, legal, technical, or consistently demanded need; the listed reports can be delivered in a later increment.
requirements.description: The system shall support periodic reports for bibliographic records with holds and without item records; items not checked out in a specified number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; and missing items. It shall also support reports for in-transit items with outstanding holds or in transit beyond a specified number of days, last-copy items, items with long call numbers, and patrons with invalid home libraries. These reports shall help reporting staff identify records and items that require operational attention.

requirements.name: Prewritten Report Templates
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft source requests delivered templates, with no explicit priority evidence.
requirements.description: The system shall include a set of prewritten report templates delivered with the product. Users shall be able to select these templates as starting points for reporting. This shall provide ready-to-use reports without requiring every report to be created from scratch.

requirements.name: Recurring Report Editing
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft specification requests editing recurring reports, with no separate priority evidence.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to edit recurring reports. Users shall be able to add or remove report selections and change email recipient addresses. This shall let users maintain recurring report configurations as their needs change.

requirements.name: Relative Date Ranges
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft specification requests the listed date-range options without an explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to run canned reports using relative date ranges. Supported ranges shall include yesterday, last week, last month, and last year. This shall make recurring time-period selections easier to apply consistently.

requirements.name: Report Recipient Address Book
requirements.priority_rationale: Requested in two sources, but one describes it as desirable and no blocking need is indicated.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an address book in which report schedulers can store and select regularly used email addresses. Users shall be able to select recipients from the address book when configuring report delivery. This shall reduce repeated entry of recipient addresses.

requirements.name: Scheduled Purging Utility
requirements.priority_rationale: The capability is requested in one email thread, with an annual end-of-year example and no stated priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to schedule the purging utility to run automatically at specified times. Scheduling shall support a recurring time such as the end of each year. This shall enable collection managers to automate planned purging or cleanup operations.

requirements.name: Sent Notice Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The capability is specified in one draft specification and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices that were sent. Reporting staff shall be able to use these reports to review notice activity. The reports shall cover all three notice categories identified in the specification.

requirements.name: Anonymized Demographic Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly requires anonymization and prohibits personally identifiable information in demographic reports, establishing a hard privacy constraint.
requirements.description: The system shall anonymize demographic statistics in reports and shall not expose personally identifiable information. This constraint shall apply whenever demographic reporting is provided. It shall allow privacy and compliance officers to use aggregated demographic results without revealing individual identities.

requirements.name: Transaction Cross Tabulation
requirements.priority_rationale: Cross-tabulation is agreed in one source and explicitly marked high priority in another; transaction grouping is also requested in a survey.
requirements.description: The system shall allow analysts and staff to group and cross-tabulate transaction reports by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location. Users shall be able to query all transaction types or filter by transaction type, including check-ins, checkouts, fines collected, and patron registrations. These dimensions shall support analysis of transaction activity at different operational and patron levels.

requirements.name: Collection Composition Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The breakdown was repeatedly requested and agreed in the source thread, and its counts and circulation totals were identified as required report data.
requirements.description: The system shall report collection and circulation metrics by genre and material format for collection managers and report users. It shall compute item counts by genre and format to show each category's percentage of the collection, and checkout totals by genre and format to show each category's percentage of total circulations. For the Shelf Space Report, users shall be able to group and aggregate results by genre, format, library, or system.

requirements.name: Comparative Period Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: Date-range filtering and comparisons were requested by collection planners and managers, and comparative circulation columns are specified in a separate reporting source.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter the Shelf Space Report by an arbitrary date range, including quarters such as Q1 and Q2. It shall support comparing report results across selected date ranges to reveal changes over time. Comparative output shall be able to include last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage differences between the periods.

requirements.name: Current-Data Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Real-time reporting is proposed in one source and specifically agreed for current-state reports in another.
requirements.description: For reports designated as requiring current data, the system shall include source transactions committed no more than five minutes before report generation begins. Each report shall display the data-through timestamp. If a source is unavailable or the five-minute freshness target cannot be met, the system shall identify the affected data and its timestamp rather than presenting it as current. Acceptance testing shall compare report contents and timestamps with committed source transactions.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting Data
requirements.priority_rationale: Historical reporting is raised in multiple sources, including a missing-feature reference and a later meeting action; the survey also specifies retention periods and aggregates.
requirements.description: The system shall support reporting on historical data, including billing data as of a specified past date and snapshots of bill amounts on that date. Retention for identifiable transaction history shall follow the configurable periods in the Financial Data Retention Policy, including applicable audit requirements and legal holds. De-identified monthly and annual aggregates shall follow the separate indefinite-retention rule for aggregate transaction information. Reports shall identify the date or period represented by the historical data.

requirements.name: Independent Item Dates
requirements.priority_rationale: Separate edit and circulation dates are requested in the reference document and a stakeholder interview, with agreement on the need to exclude circulation from edit dates.
requirements.description: The system shall provide last edit date and last circulation date as separate reportable item fields. The last edit date shall reflect the most recent bibliographic or item-record edit and shall not be updated by circulation events. Collection managers and catalogers shall be able to review editing and circulation activity independently.

requirements.name: Operational Trend Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Trend reporting is agreed for branch planning in one source and separately requested for collection decisions in another.
requirements.description: The system shall present trends over selectable time ranges to support planning and collection-management decisions. Trend reports shall show whether branches are growing or shrinking and shall support trending missing and damaged items. Users shall be able to use these results to identify changes over time and inform collection decisions.

requirements.name: Pivot Table Output
requirements.priority_rationale: Pivot-table output is requested in three separate sources, including a reference document identifying it as a missing feature.
requirements.description: The system shall provide report data in pivot-table-style output. The output shall support cross-tabulation and aggregation of report data and shall be available in a pivot-table-compatible format. Report users shall be able to use this format to examine and rearrange analytical results.

requirements.name: Staff Workflow Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: The same analysis need appears in a draft specification and meeting minutes, although neither source assigns an explicit priority.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports that allow authorized staff users and managers to review staff workflow by selected library, staff member, task type, and reporting period. Reports shall display transaction counts by task type and period, and shall identify the criteria used to produce the results. Acceptance testing shall verify the counts against a reference set of recorded transactions for each selected task type and period.

requirements.name: Transaction and Circulation Metrics
requirements.priority_rationale: The activity metrics were agreed and requested for directors and boards; circulation breakdowns are also identified as useful reporting data.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of transactions for directors, boards, and report users, including checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. Reports shall show total circulation with separate counts for checkouts, renewals, and uncataloged material circulations. Each report shall identify its reporting period and scope so results can be used to monitor library use and compare circulation measures.

requirements.name: Data Quality Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is stated in meeting minutes as necessary, but appears in only one source and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports identifying records with missing required values, invalid codes, or inconsistent relationships between records. Each result shall identify the affected record, the field or relationship that failed validation, and the validation rule. Acceptance testing shall use a reference set containing known examples of each supported issue and verify that the report identifies those examples and does not report valid reference records as failures.

requirements.name: Edited Record Counts
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is identified as missing in one reference source, with no explicit priority marker or additional source agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report counting item and bibliographic record edits during a period selected by an authorized staff user. The report shall identify the selected record type and period and return the count for that combination. Acceptance testing shall compare the reported counts with a reference set of edits whose record types and timestamps are known.

requirements.name: Hold Placement Source Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The detail is an agreed survey request from one source, with no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall record and report the placement method for each hold, with supported methods including staff desk, public computer inside a library, and remote placement. Reports shall provide both individual hold records with their placement method and aggregate hold counts grouped by placement method and reporting period. This shall allow authorized staff users to analyze hold placement patterns without combining distinct methods.

requirements.name: Library Comparison Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The side-by-side view is a specific proposed request from one source, with no explicit high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a common report view for comparing selected metrics across multiple libraries for the same reporting period. The view shall label each library, metric, and period and display results together so directors and library managers can identify differences without assembling separate reports. The measures and comparison period shall be selectable from the report's supported criteria.

requirements.name: Separate Check-In and Renewal Records and Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The unmet timestamp detail is listed in one reference source and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall record renewal transactions separately from check-in transactions and expose separate date and time values for each. Reports shall distinguish check-ins from renewals and provide separate counts and timestamps so circulation staff and analysts can verify each transaction type independently.

requirements.name: Strategic Planning Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is described across several proposed statements, but no explicit priority or agreement marker is provided.
requirements.description: The system shall provide library administrators, managers, and directors with aggregated reports for strategic planning, evaluation, and service decisions. Report users shall be able to review measures grouped by reporting period and library, and by collection where the measure supports that dimension. Reports shall label measures, groupings, and periods and shall support presentation of the resulting summaries to a library board.

requirements.name: Transaction Scope Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The report scopes are specified in one draft source and have no explicit priority or additional source agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall generate transaction reports for holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts. Users shall be able to scope these reports by patron, individual library, selected group of libraries, library system, or county. These scopes shall support analysis at both individual and broader organizational levels.

requirements.name: Voter Survey Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is listed as a missing type in one reference source, with no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report that collects and presents voter survey responses. Community engagement users shall be able to review the responses in report form. The report shall support the presentation of survey results for analysis.

requirements.name: Centralized Multi-Location Operations
requirements.priority_rationale: Centralized operation is repeated across four documents, including agreed meeting records, and establishes the architecture for serving multiple locations.
requirements.description: The system shall consolidate management processes at a central location. It shall accept input from multiple library locations and provide services to those locations. The centralized operation shall provide a single source of truth for multi-location management.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Drilldown
requirements.priority_rationale: Drilldown is agreed in the working-group summary and complements the requested overview; users could otherwise seek branch detail separately.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to drill down from the high-level capacity overview into an individual branch's detailed capacity view. The detailed view shall provide branch-level information corresponding to the overview. This shall allow users to move from system-wide review to inspection of a specific branch.

requirements.name: Consolidated Data Completeness and Freshness
requirements.priority_rationale: Meeting notes identify completeness and currency across locations as a specific challenge to consolidated operation, though no measurable threshold or explicit priority is provided.
requirements.description: For each consolidated report, the system shall identify the libraries included, the data-through timestamp for each library, and any source data unavailable to the report. Data shall be considered current only when it meets the five-minute freshness target for reports designated as requiring current data. Acceptance testing shall compare report contents with source records and verify that missing or delayed library data is identified rather than presented as complete and current.

requirements.name: Consolidated Material Volume Report
requirements.priority_rationale: The request is agreed and addresses a recurring manual task for a monthly board report, but the evidence is limited to one document and a workaround exists.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a consolidated material volume report that aggregates counts into a single report. Users shall be able to obtain the report without manually gathering the data from multiple screens. The report shall support users preparing monthly board reports.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Branch Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Requested by multiple library stakeholders and agreed; the reporting supports branch-level cleanup, with other manual coordination possible as a workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall aggregate inactive-patron counts by home library for viewing at the system level. Users shall be able to drill down from those counts to branch-level lists so they can assign cleanup tasks to specific branches. The system shall allow the inactive-patron list to be generated or configured at organizational levels such as System, Home Library, and County, as well as other levels as needed.

requirements.name: Library Capacity Overview
requirements.priority_rationale: The overview is agreed and supported by several candidate statements from the working group and branch stakeholders, including a need to see all branches at once.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an overview showing capacity information for all libraries in a library system. For each library, the overview shall display the available capacity metrics, including current load and capacity percentage. Report users shall be able to review the libraries and their metrics together to support capacity and resource decisions.

requirements.name: Library Grouping and Filtering
requirements.priority_rationale: Grouping and sorting or filtering were requested in agreed working-group material, with the source noting 286 locations and the resulting visual crowding.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to group libraries by library system or configured region and to sort and filter them by region, library type, and current load. The overview shall label the selected grouping and filters. These controls shall allow report users to navigate and compare libraries in a consortium-scale overview.

requirements.name: Library Location Report Filter
requirements.priority_rationale: The filter is agreed in the source summary and supports a specific library-level reporting need, with manual extraction as a possible workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter the material volume report by library location. When a library is selected, the report shall count only items whose location matches that library. This shall allow users to report on items at a given library at a point in time.

requirements.name: Local System Average Comparison
requirements.priority_rationale: Branch managers explicitly requested the comparison, and the source states its value for understanding local performance against the system average.
requirements.description: The system shall display a local library's Shelf Space Report results alongside the system average. Branch managers shall be able to compare local results with the system-level value. The comparison shall support review of the local library's situation in the context of the wider system.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Report Scope
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is agreed and supported by requests from multiple stakeholders, including directors who review the data quarterly and need both views.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to run the Shelf Space Report for an individual library or for the entire system. Users shall be able to select the desired scope when generating the report. The two scopes shall support local review by branch managers and system-wide review by administrators and directors.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Additions By Library
requirements.priority_rationale: This missing report was identified in one reference document for cataloging managers, with no evidence of broader demand or a blocking need.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report counting bibliographic records added by each user, grouped by library. Users shall be able to use the report to review record additions across library locations. The report shall present the counts in a form suitable for cataloging managers.

requirements.name: Circulation Counts By Patron County
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is listed as missing in one reference document for regional managers, with no further evidence of urgency or agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide circulation count reports grouped by circulation location and broken down by patron county. Regional managers shall be able to review circulation counts across locations using this county breakdown. The report shall retain the circulation location and patron county as distinct grouping dimensions.

requirements.name: Consortium Administration And Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The capability is identified for a specific administrator role in one set of meeting minutes, without a priority marker or additional supporting sources.
requirements.description: The system shall provide Global System Administrators with consortium-level capabilities to implement software changes and configurations. They shall be able to generate statistical reports for the consortium as a whole. The system shall make these capabilities available for administration and reporting across the full consortium.

requirements.name: Library Capacity Distribution Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: The need appears in one set of meeting minutes without a stated priority or evidence of broader agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports showing capacity measures and collection distribution for selected libraries. Authorized staff users shall be able to select libraries and a reporting period and compare each library's configured capacity limit with its observed collection measure. Reports shall identify the measure, limit, observed value, and difference so users can assess distribution and capacity against explicit values.

requirements.name: Library Manager Reporting Interfaces
requirements.priority_rationale: The capability is described for Library Managers in one set of meeting minutes and has no explicit priority marker or corroborating source.
requirements.description: The system shall provide Library Managers with interfaces and reporting features for supervising a single organizational unit. It shall support their contribution to the design and implementation of reports. The interfaces shall serve managers in their role overseeing a local unit.

requirements.name: Local Administrator Configuration
requirements.priority_rationale: The local configuration role is identified in one set of meeting minutes without an explicit priority or evidence of broader demand.
requirements.description: The system shall allow Local System Administrators at local branches to configure the system locally. This capability shall support local management staff in carrying out their assigned configuration role. Local configuration shall be available within the system's multi-location operation.

requirements.name: Transaction Totals By Organizational Scope
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is recorded as agreed survey input from library staff, but the source provides no response counts or explicit priority evidence.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of total transactions aggregated per patron, per library, per group of libraries, per system, and per county. Users shall be able to review totals at the scope appropriate to their reporting needs. The report shall preserve these aggregation levels as distinct options.

requirements.name: In-Transit Item Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is explicitly called critical and is agreed or requested across multiple sources; branch and delivery staff rely on it for coordination and follow-up.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an in-transit report combining transit-to and transit-from information, including items in transit to a destination library and items in transit by sending library. The report shall identify items without a recorded arrival whose departure date is more than a configurable number of days ago, with a default threshold of 7 days. Authorized staff users shall be able to view results by library or library system and sort them by due date. The report shall identify item, sending library, destination library, departure date, and arrival status to support delivery coordination and follow-up.

requirements.name: Batch Item Transfers
requirements.priority_rationale: Batch location changes and transfer utilities are requested in multiple documents by cataloging, logistics, and library staff; manual record updates offer a workaround.
