requirements.description: The system shall provide staff with a utility to transfer batches of selected items between branches and to special locations, including mobile units and outreach collections. The utility shall update each selected item's location to the destination location as part of the transfer. It shall support changing item records in batches, rather than requiring staff to update each location individually.

requirements.name: Delayed Transfer Alerts
requirements.priority_rationale: The alert is a useful operational capability requested in one source, but the evidence does not establish a critical or mandatory need.
requirements.description: The system shall notify configured recipients when a transfer has no recorded arrival after its configured delay threshold or when a transfer operation records a failure or invalid transfer status. Configuration shall specify the delay threshold, recipient roles or addresses, and notification channel; the system shall identify the affected item, sending and destination libraries, detected condition, and detection time. The system shall retry a failed notification and retain its delivery status until delivery succeeds or an authorized staff user is alerted to intervene. Acceptance testing shall verify each condition, configured recipient and channel, and failed-delivery handling.

requirements.name: Missing and Damaged Item Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: Branch-level reporting is agreed as crucial for accountability and requested for inventory audits; additional filters and incident details support trending and collection decisions.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of missing and damaged items by library, including counts grouped by library and item-level results. Authorized staff users shall be able to select date ranges and filter by status, including missing, lost, and long overdue, and review item condition notes. Reports shall support auditing and collection decisions, including identifying items with repeated incidents for replacement or relocation.

requirements.name: Scheduled Transfer Reversion
requirements.priority_rationale: Timed reversion is requested across several sources, including a survey, and supports temporary transfers; staff may otherwise revert locations manually.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized staff to return transferred items to their original location automatically after a configurable period or on a specified event, such as an item's status changing to "returned" or "sold". For temporary transfers to an event or program, staff shall be able to specify an end date that triggers reversion. The system shall support scheduled processing of these time- and event-based rules, while leaving an item at its destination if it has been checked out there. Staff shall also be able to revert an item to its original location when needed.

requirements.name: Transfer Audit History
requirements.priority_rationale: Transfer logging and item-level history are requested by different stakeholders in the same source; audit and accountability are important, though some history may be tracked manually.
requirements.description: The system shall record transfer actions and item location changes for audit purposes, including who performed each transfer and when. It shall retain transfer history for each item, including transfer timestamps and the number of times the item has been transferred. Authorized users shall be able to review this history to support auditing and collection decisions.

requirements.name: Item Status Conversion Report
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is requested in one draft specification and supports a specific cataloging workflow.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report to assist authorized staff users with batch conversion of item statuses. The report shall identify the items and their current statuses relevant to the intended status change, allowing staff to review the items before performing the batch conversion. This requirement covers the status-conversion report, not authorization or execution safeguards for the conversion operation.

requirements.name: Printable Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.priority_rationale: Pull lists are requested in two documents as a transfer mechanism, but staff can prepare retrieval lists by other means.
requirements.description: The system shall generate a printable pull list of items to be moved in a transfer batch. Staff shall be able to use the list to retrieve the items for physical transfer. This shall support the picking and logistics work that accompanies a transfer.

requirements.name: Printable Transit Labels
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a single-source operational convenience that can be supported by other labeling methods if not delivered.
requirements.description: The system shall generate printable transit labels for items in a transfer. Each label shall include a barcode associated with the item. Staff shall be able to print the labels for use while handling and routing transferred items.

requirements.name: Separate Report Documentation
requirements.priority_rationale: The reports working group agreed to track the two reports separately in documentation; this is a specific documentation need rather than a system operation.
requirements.description: The system documentation shall record the Missing and Damaged Items report and the In-Transit Items report as separate entries. It shall preserve their distinction even though both reports relate to item movement or condition. This shall make each report requirement identifiable and trackable in the documentation.

requirements.name: Transfer Preview Confirmation
requirements.priority_rationale: A single source proposes a concrete safeguard that reduces transfer errors; staff can otherwise check batches manually.
requirements.description: Before executing a transfer batch, the system shall show staff a preview and request confirmation. The preview shall state the number of items to be moved and the source and destination locations. This shall give staff an opportunity to catch an incorrect selection or destination before changes are made.

requirements.name: Transfer Undo
requirements.priority_rationale: Undo is requested in one source as protection against mistakes, while manual correction provides a workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized users to undo a recent transfer operation. Undo shall reverse the location changes made by that operation. This shall enable staff to recover from an accidental transfer without correcting each item individually.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Shipment Processing
requirements.priority_rationale: This efficiency need comes from one stakeholder interview and is useful for a specific shipment workflow, but is not described as blocking other transfers.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a bulk distribution and processing mode for uncataloged shipments. It shall enable staff to distribute these shipments quickly while minimizing the per-item labor required at branches. This capability shall support rapid processing before items are cataloged.

requirements.name: Indirect Patron Access to Report Output
requirements.priority_rationale: This access model appears in one meeting-minutes source and is framed as a possible indirect use rather than a core operational need.
requirements.description: The system shall allow libraries to display selected report output on screens intended for patrons without providing patrons with access to reporting functions or underlying report data. Patron interactions with library services shall remain primarily through the OPAC. Acceptance testing shall verify that displayed output contains only the information selected for public display and does not expose restricted patron information.

requirements.name: Deletion Activity Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed reporting request was called an administrative requirement and described as something stakeholders “absolutely need” for compliance; it is supported by several stakeholders and a survey request from 27% of respondents.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports and queries over deletion audit records so administrators can monitor deletion activity and investigate specific events. Reports shall show total deletions by month, quarter, or year; deletions by record type (including items, patrons, and other records); deletions by location; and the users with the most deletions, with views per system and per location. Users shall be able to filter or aggregate results by date range, user, and record type, retrieve entries for a specific record_id, and review deletion reasons; the system shall count and track deletions per location and system.

requirements.name: Last-Item Identification and Pre-Deletion Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed requirement is explicitly marked “CRITICAL,” and multiple participants requested both per-library and per-system views to avoid deleting a consortium's only copy.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report identifying items that are the last item within a selected library, library system, or consortium scope. Authorized staff users shall be able to review current last-item status and use the report in a pre-deletion workflow before an authorized purge. Results shall provide item identifiers and actionable details to support cataloging, preservation, and external-catalog decisions.

requirements.name: Batch Item Status Conversion
requirements.priority_rationale: Cataloging staff described batch conversion as a major time-saving need, and the item-report specification also includes items to be converted; the sources indicate substantial operational benefit.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized staff members to select multiple items and change their status in one batch operation, including changing items from missing to discard/weed. Before applying the change, the system shall show the selected item count and the source and destination statuses and require confirmation. Acceptance testing shall verify that the change applies only to the selected items and that items with an invalid status transition are identified rather than silently changed.

requirements.name: Bulk Related Record Deletion
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is agreed across an email thread and repeated in a stakeholder interview and draft specification; a manual workaround exists but is described as time-consuming.
requirements.description: The system shall provide an efficient utility for authorized cataloging staff and administrators to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries. The utility shall also identify and delete bibliographic or other records that have no item records attached. These operations shall support cleanup of related and orphaned records without requiring staff to locate and delete each record through a slow manual process.

requirements.name: Customizable Weeding Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: Weeding reports are described as frequently used and as the interviewee’s most-used report type, with related needs appearing in both a draft specification and stakeholder sources.
requirements.description: The system shall provide weeding reports that identify items for review using criteria configurable by authorized report users. Criteria shall include an item remaining in the missing status for more than a configurable number of months and items in the discard/weed status, as defined by the Library Automation System's status codes. Each report shall include the date of the item's last circulation. A report shall identify items for review only; it shall not itself purge or delete items.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Trail
requirements.priority_rationale: Agreed audit needs appear in multiple stakeholder communications and support accountability and compliance, although no source marks the audit trail as critical or mandatory.
requirements.description: The system shall maintain persistent audit records for purge-related deletions and denied deletion attempts so administrators and auditors can establish what happened and who performed or attempted the action. Each deletion record shall include record_type, record_id, deleted_by, deleted_at, and location, and the audit trail shall identify the actor and timestamp for denied attempts. The system shall support optionally recording an item's status before deletion; deletion reasons shall be captured as specified in Deletion Activity Reporting.

requirements.name: Deletion Confirmation Step
requirements.priority_rationale: The confirmation safeguard was agreed by cataloging staff and administrators and addresses the significant risk of unintended deletion, although it is stated in one source.
requirements.description: The system shall require users to complete a separate, explicit confirmation step before performing deletions identified by purge reports. The confirmation shall occur after candidate identification and review, rather than being implicit in viewing or running a report. This safeguard shall help prevent accidental execution of purge actions.

requirements.name: Read-Only Purge Preview
requirements.priority_rationale: The safeguard was agreed by cataloging staff and managers and reduces the risk of accidental deletion, though only one source explicitly requests this preview.
requirements.description: The system shall display purge candidates in a read-only preview before deletion. Users shall be able to review the candidate report without being able to delete records directly from that report. This separation shall help staff inspect proposed purge actions before proceeding to a deletion operation.

requirements.name: Deleted Last-Item Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is requested in draft specifications to support external catalog maintenance, but the evidence is limited to one source and no critical priority marker is given.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report listing items that were purged even though they were the last item owned within the relevant library system. The report shall identify each item and the affected library system so authorized staff users can review the records and update WorldCat or other external catalog records after the purge.

requirements.name: Predefined Item Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The report catalogue is specified in a single draft specification and provides useful operational coverage, but no evidence marks the full catalogue as critical.
requirements.description: The system shall provide predefined item reports for Items Added Count, List of Items Added, Items Edited Count, Items Count, Items Deleted Count, Lists by Fines Stopped Reason, Items Currently Checked Out, Items more than a configurable number of days overdue, Items marked longoverdue, Long Overdue lists, Items in Transit by sending and destination library, Claims returned, Lists by Creation Date Range, Lists with status Missing, Lists by Total Use Count thresholds, a Last Copy Report, a Weeding Report showing date of last circulation and number of circulations, Lists with a specified value in the bibliographic record, Age of collection by call number or shelving location, Price value of collection by call number or shelving location, and Items to be Converted. The reports shall support collection management and operational review, including weeding and identifying items for batch status conversion.

requirements.name: Accounting and Audit Compliance
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly says reports and archiving must comply with accounting and governmental auditing requirements.
requirements.description: The system shall support financial reports and archived financial data in compliance with applicable accounting and governmental auditing requirements. Before compliance acceptance, the project shall identify the governing accounting standards and applicable state, county, and municipal audit provisions in a controlled compliance register, with exact document, section, and version references. Acceptance testing shall verify the applicable reporting and retention obligations against that approved register.

requirements.name: Auditable Payment Ledger
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed finance and auditor requirement explicitly marks payment traceability as critical for reconciliation; a related draft also requests transaction tracking and verification.
requirements.description: The system shall maintain an auditable ledger of patron payments that identifies each payment and the specific charge or charges to which it was applied. Finance staff and auditors shall be able to use the ledger and related tools or reports to track and verify financial transactions. The ledger shall provide traceability needed to reconcile accounts.

requirements.name: Financial Data Retention Policy
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed source identifies legally or policy-required retention, including a seven-year audit period, and explicitly requires the system to enforce it.
requirements.description: The system shall enforce configurable retention periods by financial data category. Where the approved legal or policy requirement specifies a seven-year audit period, the system shall apply that period to the applicable records; other categories shall use their approved periods. De-identified aggregate transaction information shall be governed by the applicable policy and law, not assumed to be exempt from deletion. An authorized legal hold shall suspend deletion for affected records, and the system shall record policy changes and deletion actions. The approved retention schedule shall identify the governing authority and applicable data categories before compliance acceptance.

requirements.name: Bills and Debt Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The specified report set supports routine finance work, but it is requested in one draft source and has no explicit high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide bills reports for staff members and finance staff members. The reports shall include bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, forgiven amounts, payments made using work credit, payments made using goods credit, detailed voids, and aged debt. Each report shall label these categories separately so staff members can distinguish payments, credits, and forgiven amounts when reviewing outstanding bills and payment activity.

requirements.name: De-Identified Aggregate Transaction Retention
requirements.priority_rationale: Indefinite retention is explicitly requested in the draft specification, though it appears in only one source.
requirements.description: The system shall retain monthly and annual aggregate transaction information only after it has been de-identified so it cannot identify a patron. Retention and deletion of these aggregates shall follow the applicable approved retention policy and legal requirements; this requirement does not establish indefinite retention or override a legal hold. The system shall record retention-policy changes and any resulting deletion actions.

requirements.name: Financial Data Joining
requirements.priority_rationale: The later source records an agreed need from finance and reporting staff to join the two financial data sources for reporting.
requirements.description: The system shall allow reporting users to join financial data associated with patron records to financial data associated with item records. The joined data shall be usable to combine or correlate those sources in financial reports. This supports reporting across the patron and item dimensions of financial activity.

requirements.name: Financial Record Associations
requirements.priority_rationale: The need appears in both the draft specification and a later agreed source, with finance and reporting staff identified as stakeholders.
requirements.description: The system shall associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with the relevant patron and item records. Finance staff members and report users shall be able to use these associations when reviewing financial activity. Acceptance testing shall verify that each supported transaction type is linked to the correct patron and item records when those records exist.

requirements.name: Financial Summary and Library Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The reporting needs are described across draft and later agreed sources, with finance, branch, and director stakeholders identified; the reports support routine reconciliation and budget monitoring.
requirements.description: The system shall provide financial reports for finance staff, authorized staff users at libraries, and library directors. Reports shall show patron account balances by patron, home library, and library system; fines and charges by period and charge type; fines waived by period and library; and payments by period, payment instrument, and collection channel. The reports shall support end-of-month and other reporting by identifying the library where a payment was collected and the library to which it is attributed.

requirements.name: Financial Transaction Update Latency
requirements.priority_rationale: The need was agreed by front desk and finance staff, who specifically report that delayed updates impede their work.
requirements.description: The system shall reflect a committed financial transaction, including a front-desk payment, in account balances and reports designated as current within five minutes of the transaction commit. Such reports shall display their data-through timestamp. If the transaction is not available within that interval, the system shall identify the affected data as delayed rather than presenting it as current. Acceptance testing shall measure elapsed time from transaction commit to report availability.

requirements.name: Patron Balance Threshold Queries
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed source says this was repeatedly requested and that manual retrieval currently takes too long, indicating an important daily-work need with a manual workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall allow an authorized staff user to query patron accounts whose balances exceed a threshold amount specified for each query. The result shall identify the patron accounts meeting the threshold and support review of accounts requiring attention. The query shall not use a fixed threshold.

requirements.name: Editable Financial Information
requirements.priority_rationale: Ease of updating is requested in one draft source without a specific workflow, urgency marker, or evidence of broader agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized staff members to select a financial record, edit permitted fields, review the proposed changes, and save or cancel the update. The system shall validate required fields before saving and identify validation failures to the staff member. Acceptance testing shall verify that authorized staff members can update permitted fields and that unauthorized changes are rejected.

requirements.name: Historical Bill Snapshots
requirements.priority_rationale: The capability is listed as an unmet need in one reference document, without an explicit high-priority marker or broader stakeholder agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a snapshot bills report that shows bill states as they existed at earlier points in time. Finance and reporting users shall be able to review historical snapshots rather than only current bill states. This supports investigation and comparison of past financial positions.

requirements.name: Circulation Activity Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Activity reporting is requested in a draft specification and survey results, with specific breakdowns requested by library staff; a manual reporting workaround is possible.
requirements.description: The system shall provide activity reports showing counts of check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. It shall also report transaction types including fines collected and patron registrations, as well as check-in counts by method, including book drop, terminal, and self-service. The system shall report check-out and renewal types separately, including staff checkout, self checkout, staff renewal, self checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal, so staff and management can understand circulation activity and service use.

requirements.name: Collection Value Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Value reporting is requested in a draft specification and an agreed finance/staff email, which identifies purchase price data already present in item records.
requirements.description: The system shall generate reports of monetary item value using the purchase price field in item records, querying and aggregating that field as needed. Users shall be able to report value for the entire collection or a selected portion, with filters including item status, material type, and collection membership; examples include long-overdue items and children's DVDs. The system shall also report collection value aggregated by call number ranges to support collection and finance analysis.

requirements.name: Collection Volume History
requirements.priority_rationale: The collection history capability is requested across multiple sources and supports important board and assessment reporting, but a temporary workaround exists and the evidence does not establish a mandatory constraint.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a collection volume report for a specified library and date or point in time, including historical counts rather than only current values. The report shall distinguish new acquisitions, items on the shelf, and items out in circulation, and shall include checked-out items in the total volume. It shall use the item acquisition date for acquisition and time-range reporting, show changes over time, and allow recent-addition intervals such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days. Users shall be able to report on acquisitions, shelf items, and circulating items with category breakdowns including total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

requirements.name: Library Capacity Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: Branch capacity analysis is requested in the draft specification and technical email, and meeting minutes state that inventory and capacity reports are used daily.
requirements.description: The system shall provide capacity reports for selected libraries and a consolidated view across selected libraries. Reports shall identify each library, the configured capacity measure, the observed value, the capacity limit, and the difference between the observed value and limit. Authorized staff users shall be able to select the reporting scope and period; acceptance testing shall verify displayed values against configured limits and reference inventory data.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Utilization Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: The comparison is requested in multiple sources, including an agreed working-group summary and a stakeholder interview, and is described as important for collection management.
requirements.description: The system shall provide shelf-space utilization reports for each genre and format, comparing the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Reports shall be runnable for an individual library and for the library system. The system shall estimate shelf space by genre and format using item dimensions when available and item count as a proxy when dimensions are unavailable, so planners can assess the percentage of shelf space occupied.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Inventory
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is described in both a draft specification and a stakeholder interview, with concrete operational needs for distribution and inventory tracking.
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to track uncataloged material as inventory even when individual bibliographic records are unavailable. It shall support material such as paperback books and children's board books, and shall support quick distribution with minimal branch labor. This inventory capability shall allow branch staff and collection managers to control and locate uncataloged material.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Usage
requirements.priority_rationale: Transaction counting is requested in both a draft specification and a stakeholder interview, and the interview also requests usage information.
requirements.description: The system shall count transactions involving uncataloged material and include those counts in circulation statistics and reports. It shall record and report how uncataloged material is used so staff can evaluate its circulation and use. The system shall support this reporting even when the material is not fully cataloged.

requirements.name: Circulation Count Breakdowns
requirements.priority_rationale: Four distinct report types are listed as missing or partially available in one reference source, but no priority marker or broad stakeholder agreement is stated.
requirements.description: The system shall provide circulation count reports grouped by patron age demographic, circulation modifier, Dewey classification, and MARC field values. Users shall be able to select the relevant breakdown when reviewing circulation counts. These reports shall support collection and circulation analysis using the classification and record data identified in the sources.

requirements.name: Claims Returned Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: This report is listed as unavailable in one reference source, with no stated priority marker or supporting source.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a Claims Returned report listing items that patrons have claimed to have returned. Circulation staff shall be able to use the report to identify and review those items. The report shall make claims-returned information available as a distinct report type.

requirements.name: Collection Age By Call Number
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is listed as missing in one reference source and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report showing the age of the collection aggregated by call number ranges. Collection managers shall be able to use the report to assess the age profile of holdings across those ranges. The report shall use collection item data to calculate the grouped results.

requirements.name: Collection Usage Analysis
requirements.priority_rationale: The need appears in two sources, but neither identifies a priority marker or a specific operational blocker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide collection managers and librarians with reports and analysis tools for examining the library collection and how patrons use it. The analysis shall support collection-management decisions by making collection holdings and patron use available for review. It shall allow users to analyze collection usage without requiring a specific report format.

requirements.name: Configurable Capacity Metrics
requirements.priority_rationale: A working-group discussion identifies capacity metrics as an input needed for the interface, but the request remains questioned and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized users to define and configure the metrics used to represent capacity. Supported metric choices shall include item count versus shelf space, physical item count versus a configured limit, and circulation volume versus processing capacity. The system shall use the selected metric when presenting capacity information so that branches can apply a consistent, meaningful definition of capacity.

requirements.name: Item Use Count Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Use counts and filtering by a specified count are requested in a draft specification and a reference report list, without explicit priority markers.
requirements.description: The system shall maintain and report total use counts for items. It shall also provide use counts by date range, including fiscal-year and monthly counts. Collection analysts shall be able to identify items matching a specified total use count.

requirements.name: Items By Creation Date
requirements.priority_rationale: This report is listed as unavailable in one reference source and has no explicit priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report listing items created within a specified creation-date range. Inventory managers shall be able to use the report to identify items added during the selected period. The report shall allow the user to specify the date range used to select items.

requirements.name: Items By Fines Stopped
requirements.priority_rationale: This report is listed as unavailable in one reference source, with no additional evidence of priority.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report listing items grouped by the reason fines were stopped. Circulation and finance staff shall be able to review the items and their associated reasons. The report shall make the fines-stopped reason available as a grouping criterion.

requirements.name: Last Circulation Date
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a single survey request with no explicit priority marker or evidence of broad agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall indicate the last circulation date on item reports. Collection and circulation staff shall be able to use this date when reviewing individual items. The report shall display the date associated with the item's most recent circulation.

requirements.name: Overdue Items With Contact
requirements.priority_rationale: The report is listed as unavailable in one reference source; the overdue threshold is specified as configurable but no priority marker is provided.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report of items that are more than a user-specified number of days overdue. The report shall include patron contact information for each item. Circulation staff shall be able to use the report to identify overdue items requiring follow-up.

requirements.name: Unfilled and Stale Holds Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Stale holds are listed as an unavailable report type in one reference source, with no stated priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for unfilled holds and stale holds. An unfilled hold is a hold that has not been fulfilled; a stale hold is an unfilled hold that has remained unfulfilled beyond a report-user-configurable age threshold. Report users shall be able to select the threshold and identify which category each result meets. Acceptance testing shall verify that all stale holds are included among unfilled holds and that unfilled holds below the threshold are not classified as stale.

requirements.name: Volume Category Breakdowns
requirements.priority_rationale: The cited evidence is primarily a draft or email request and does not establish a legal, technical, mandatory, or consistently demanded need. The capability is useful but can be delivered after core reporting.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to break down collection volume by categories including total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books. It shall support grouping by category attributes such as fiction or non-fiction and format, and shall allow each library to customize the categories used. The report shall show hold counts per category so collection managers can examine volume using categories relevant to their library.

requirements.name: Configurable Color-Coded Capacity Status
requirements.priority_rationale: Color coding is proposed as a usability enhancement in one source, with no evidence that it is required for core operation.
requirements.description: The system shall display capacity status using green, yellow, and red indicators based on library-configured capacity thresholds. The configuration shall define the numeric boundary for each status, with green below the yellow boundary, yellow from that boundary to the red boundary, and red at or above the red boundary. Acceptance testing shall verify the displayed status immediately below, at, and above each configured boundary.

requirements.name: Patron Characteristic Filtering and Grouping
requirements.priority_rationale: The reporting working group agreed on these characteristics, and a stakeholder explicitly called the capability essential; patron-type categories are also identified as important.
requirements.description: The system shall allow report users to filter and group queries and reports by patron age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home library, patron type, and preferred language. Patron type shall support categories such as adult, juvenile, senior, and student. Acceptance testing shall verify that each characteristic can be selected as a filter and grouping field and that results reflect the selected criteria.

requirements.name: Combined Demographic Activity Filters
requirements.priority_rationale: The combined-filter need was agreed in an email thread, and technical feasibility was confirmed, but it appears in one source.
requirements.description: The system shall let report users combine demographic criteria with activity-based conditions in a single query. Conditions shall support examples such as juvenile patrons in zip code 30505 who have not checked anything out in six months. This shall allow users to identify targeted patron groups without running separate reports and manually combining results.

requirements.name: Configurable Age-Based Reporting
requirements.priority_rationale: Age calculation feasibility was confirmed and configurable age ranges were agreed in the same reporting discussion, though no mandatory marker or broad survey support is given.
requirements.description: The system shall calculate a patron's age at query time from the stored birth_date field. Report users shall be able to configure age ranges for each report and use those ranges for filtering and grouping. Configurable examples include 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 and 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.

requirements.name: Configurable Inactive Patron Reports
requirements.priority_rationale: The inactive-patron report is requested in multiple sources and the threshold is agreed as configurable; a listed report is also identified as unavailable.
requirements.description: The system shall generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a number of days specified by a report user. The report user shall be able to enter any number of days and select presets of 30, 90, 180, or 365 days, with report scope options including library system, home library, and county. The output shall identify the selected inactivity threshold and the patron records meeting it.

requirements.name: Demographic Statistics and Privacy
requirements.priority_rationale: Demographic analysis is requested across a draft specification, meeting minutes, email, and survey; the sources also explicitly call for anonymized data, but do not mark the overall capability mandatory.
requirements.description: The system shall provide demographic statistics to support program planning and analysis of patron demographics and interests. Statistics shall include transactions by geographic region, county, city, ZIP code, and age range, as well as patron and circulation aggregates grouped by demographic fields. The system shall use de-identified data for these statistics and shall not expose patron-identifying information in the reported results.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Exclusion Criteria
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed email thread gives an explicit list of exclusion categories for report users, but the request is from one source.
requirements.description: The system shall let users exclude selected patron categories from inactive-patron reports. Exclusion criteria shall include do-not-disturb flags, VIP status, staff membership, and opting out of communications. This shall allow users to limit report results to patrons appropriate for the intended follow-up.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Mailing Addresses
requirements.priority_rationale: Outreach staff explicitly request current mailing addresses for a stated postcard workflow in an agreed source.
requirements.description: The system shall include each inactive patron's current mailing address in the inactive-patron report. The address shall be available to outreach staff using the report to mail postcards. The report shall use the patron's current address information.

requirements.name: Inactive Report CSV Export
requirements.priority_rationale: The CSV format and outreach-system use are explicitly requested by multiple stakeholders in an agreed email thread.
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to export the inactive-patron report as a CSV file. The export shall contain the report results in a format suitable for upload to outreach systems. This shall support the stated workflow of using the report for patron outreach.

requirements.name: Null Values In Report Results
requirements.priority_rationale: The reporting working group agreed that null values should be included, with multiple participants supporting the approach to prevent misleading results.
requirements.description: The system shall include records with null values for optional patron fields in report results rather than silently excluding those records. The report shall display missing values explicitly as null. This shall help users interpret results without misleading omissions caused by incomplete patron data.

requirements.name: Patron Activity Data Integration
requirements.priority_rationale: Multiple participants agreed that inactivity must account for electronic activity as well as circulation, and implementer notes identify the combined query needed to retrieve it.
requirements.description: The system shall determine each patron's most recent activity date using circulation transactions and available electronic-activity data from the relevant tables. Electronic activity shall include OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and digital-collection access when integrated. The system shall query OPAC patron data, including holds and circulation, and combine the sources to support reporting.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior Analytics
requirements.priority_rationale: Similar behavior-analysis needs and example metrics appear in both a draft specification and survey results, indicating support across two sources.
requirements.description: The system shall produce statistics to help users understand and predict patron behavior and use of materials. Metrics shall include average time to return an item, renewal likelihood or probability, and the percentage of check-outs that are renewals. Users shall be able to analyze the renewal percentage for a particular branch.

requirements.name: Patron Reporting Data Fields
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed technical response confirms these fields exist in the patron table and are straightforward to query, supporting several reporting needs.
requirements.description: The system shall store and make available the patron fields needed for reporting: zip code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, preferred language, and birth_date. These fields shall be accessible to patron reports and queries. The birth_date field shall support age calculation.

requirements.name: Aged Debt Report Field Decision
requirements.priority_rationale: A reference document identifies the report as partially available and needing enhancement, but provides no field details or evidence of broader agreement.
requirements.description: This item is a stakeholder decision, not a current software requirement: stakeholders shall approve and document the additional fields required for the Aged Debt report before the report enhancement is specified. The decision record shall identify each field, its definition, source data, and expected output behavior. No implementation or acceptance claim for additional fields is made until that controlled decision is approved.

requirements.name: Outstanding Fines Inactivity Flags
requirements.priority_rationale: The request to flag inactive patrons with fines is agreed in one email thread, but the source frames it as a proposed handling distinction.
requirements.description: The system shall identify inactive patrons who have outstanding fines in inactive-patron report results. It shall flag those accounts so staff can distinguish them from other inactive patrons. This shall support handling those accounts differently during follow-up.

requirements.name: Patron Data Completeness Indicators
requirements.priority_rationale: A report completeness indicator is proposed in one email thread, with examples but no explicit priority or broader agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall show the completeness of selected patron fields in report outputs. Users shall be able to see how many records lack fields such as zip code or preferred language. This shall help users assess whether those fields are populated consistently before interpreting report results.

requirements.name: Patron Report Catalog
requirements.priority_rationale: The full report catalog appears in one draft specification and is proposed without a priority marker or evidence of stakeholder agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall provide the requested patron-report set for management and report users. The set shall include Patron Count; Patron Added Count by Month; New Patron Count by Demographic Category; counts by age demographic, county, county/city/zip, home library, profile group, and survey answer; lists by survey answer, expiration date, barred status, inactive status, and wording in notes; and Voter Survey Responses County by Week. The set shall also include staff-account lists showing the date of last password change and account expiration.

requirements.name: Per-Patron Transaction Counts
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is stated in one draft specification without an explicit priority or evidence of wider agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall show the number of check-outs and placed holds for each patron in transaction reports. Users shall be able to review both counts in the report results. This shall support analysis of patron transaction activity at the individual-patron level.

requirements.name: Client Platform and Browser Compatibility
requirements.priority_rationale: Client access is explicitly marked high priority, and the browser versions are agreed across sources; one source cites the cost of upgrading more than 200 computers.
requirements.description: The system shall be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client. When browser access is used, the system shall support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later. Acceptance testing shall verify access using the specified minimum browser versions where those platforms are part of the deployment baseline.

requirements.name: Consortium Capacity
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly marks this capacity requirement high priority and gives concrete consortium scale figures.
requirements.description: The system shall support consortium operations across at least 286 libraries, 17 million annual circulations, and the purchasing and processing of more than 900,000 items annually. Acceptance testing shall load representative records at these stated volumes and verify that reports can query the full consortium data set without data loss or errors. These figures define the minimum operational scale the system must accommodate.

requirements.name: Online-Hours Workload Continuity
requirements.priority_rationale: Open-hours processing is marked high priority in one source and identified as a key requirement in another; survey feedback also reports slow reports during busy hours.
requirements.description: The system shall allow reports to run during open hours without disrupting circulation or OPAC use. Under the consortium workload capacity specified for acceptance testing, the 95th-percentile response time for interactive circulation and OPAC requests shall not exceed two seconds, excluding network latency outside the system boundary. Long-running reports shall be queued and processed in the background. Acceptance testing shall compare interactive response times with and without the representative reporting workload.

requirements.name: OPAC Non-Interference
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is supported by multiple sources, including an agreed statement that reporting absolutely cannot constrain the OPAC and a source marking OPAC protection high priority.
requirements.description: The system shall be architected and operated so that reporting activity does not constrain OPAC functionality or degrade catalog responsiveness for patrons. Heavy reporting queries shall not slow down the OPAC. Reporting shall preserve the OPAC's ability to provide its existing features.

requirements.name: Privacy-Preserving Transaction Archive
requirements.priority_rationale: The sources identify state-law retention and patron privacy as compliance requirements, including an explicit legal-constraint signal.
requirements.description: The system shall archive transaction data in a form that protects patron privacy and follows the retention periods established for applicable data categories in REQ-ACCT-003. The archive shall not retain personally identifiable patron information where the approved privacy policy requires de-identification. The project compliance baseline shall identify the governing state-law or approved policy provision and its retention period before compliance acceptance; this requirement does not introduce an unspecified period such as “X years.”

requirements.name: Privacy-Protected Transaction Archive
requirements.priority_rationale: The source marks this as high priority and cites State Law and privacy officers as evidence of a legal and privacy obligation.
requirements.description: The system shall archive transaction data in a form that protects patron privacy as required by the applicable law and approved privacy policy. Before compliance acceptance, the project shall identify the governing law or policy, including exact document, section, and version references, in a controlled compliance register. The archive shall support approved demographic statistics without exposing personally identifiable patron information, and acceptance testing shall verify those privacy controls against the register.

requirements.name: Relational Database Backend
requirements.priority_rationale: The relational backend is explicitly marked high priority and mandatory in a source, and PostgreSQL compatibility is supported by the stated existing environment.
requirements.description: The system shall use a fully relational database backend and operate against a fully relational database schema. It shall be compatible with PostgreSQL, including the stated current environment of PostgreSQL 8.3. This constraint shall align the reporting system with the existing database environment.

requirements.name: System Accessibility
requirements.priority_rationale: Section 508 is identified as mandatory and a legal requirement, with additional accessibility requests from multiple sources.
requirements.description: The system, including reporting functions, online help, and HTML report output, shall comply with Section 508 and applicable accessibility standards. It shall support screen-reading software, including JAWS and NVDA, screen-magnification software, including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies. Acceptance testing shall assess the system's user-facing functions against the applicable accessibility criteria and verify access using the identified assistive technologies.

requirements.name: Administrative Error Feedback
requirements.priority_rationale: Error feedback is requested in multiple sources, including an agreed source with concrete diagnostic details; the source material also identifies staff need when reports fail.
requirements.description: The system shall provide users with clear, high-level error reporting and feedback when operations or reports fail. For administrators, it shall also provide query-specific details, including the table, field, and kind of error when available. This feedback shall help users understand failures and help administrators diagnose and resolve them.

requirements.name: Enterprise Deployment Assumptions
requirements.priority_rationale: Enterprise membership is agreed or stated in three sources, and centralized connectivity and infrastructure assumptions are documented for IT operations.
requirements.description: The system shall operate as part of an enterprise-level Library Automation System and use the enterprise infrastructure on which it depends. The deployment shall support centralized operation across multiple locations and rely on reliable network connectivity between those locations and central servers. The enterprise infrastructure assumption includes redundant servers and backups.

requirements.name: Enterprise Library Automation System Integration
requirements.priority_rationale: Integration with the enterprise ILS and its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules is described across three sources, including an agreed assumption.
requirements.description: The system shall integrate with the enterprise Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and shall not replace their operational functions. The Library Automation System shall remain the system of record for its data; the reporting system shall read the data required for reporting through supported interfaces or read-only access. The implementation shall document the interfaces, data ownership, supported read operations, and synchronization behavior for each module.

requirements.name: Environment Separation and Configuration Migration
requirements.priority_rationale: Environment separation and migration are requested across multiple sources, including an agreed description of existing environments; a manual configuration transfer is a possible temporary workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments so that development and training work does not affect production. Authorized report users shall be able to export and import report templates, saved queries, permission settings, and other report configurations between environments. Acceptance testing shall verify that each artifact type can be migrated and that imported configurations retain their settings and permissions without changing production until explicitly applied.

requirements.name: Isolated Training Environment
requirements.priority_rationale: The need appears in an interview and was subsequently agreed in meeting notes, with production-data protection emphasized.
requirements.description: The system shall provide a training environment in which new staff can practice running reports. The training environment shall be separate from production and shall prevent practice or experimentation from affecting production data. This shall allow staff to learn report functions without risking live records.

requirements.name: Linux and Solaris Server Compatibility
requirements.priority_rationale: Linux and Solaris support is agreed as acceptable in one source and requested in another, with specific platform versions and hardware stated by the technical stakeholder.
requirements.description: The system shall be deployable and operable on Linux or Solaris servers. Supported platform constraints include Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware, as specified by the sources. The approved deployment baseline shall identify the selected server platform and verify that the system's supported functionality operates on it.

requirements.name: Management Reporting Scope
requirements.priority_rationale: The scope boundary is established in agreed meeting material and defines which system functions belong in this reporting effort.
requirements.description: The system's reporting scope shall focus on Management Processes: reports and analysis tools used by managers, administrators, and staff for planning, evaluation, and oversight. It shall exclude day-to-day patron-facing OPAC and circulation client functions. Acquisitions and Cataloging shall be specified separately rather than within the Management Processes reports specification.

requirements.name: Queued Background Report Processing
requirements.priority_rationale: Background processing is agreed or requested in three sources, with database contention and performance identified as major concerns; reports can otherwise be run interactively as a workaround.
requirements.description: The system shall queue complex and long-running report jobs and process them in the background, separately from interactive sessions. A report user shall receive job status within five seconds of submission, and the queue shall accept at least 100 pending jobs without blocking submission or interactive operations. Report execution shall not directly block circulation or other interactive operations; acceptance testing shall verify that circulation response times remain within the target specified for online-hours workload continuity. Results for the inactive-patrons report shall be cached for the same parameters and data snapshot, with the cache invalidated when that snapshot changes.

requirements.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
requirements.priority_rationale: The read-only boundary is agreed in one source and provides a clear integration constraint for reporting on OPAC-related data.
requirements.description: The system shall query OPAC-related data for patron-created holds and circulation transactions when needed for reporting. It shall not modify OPAC data. This read-only access shall allow reporting to use relevant patron activity data while preserving the OPAC as the source of that data.

requirements.name: Relational Database Compatibility
requirements.priority_rationale: The relational-model constraint was stated as an agreed architectural requirement by a systems administrator.
requirements.description: The system shall operate within and use the relational database structure. Its architecture shall not violate or work against the relational model. This constraint shall preserve compatibility with the agreed database structure.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Logging
requirements.priority_rationale: This was agreed in one source, but no legal mandate, high-priority marker, or broader stakeholder agreement is stated.
requirements.description: The system shall record database deletions in a deletion audit table. It shall implement database-triggered logging so that deletions are captured when they occur. The audit record shall support administrators who need to review deletion activity.

requirements.name: Large Dataset Report Performance
requirements.priority_rationale: One source raises an explicit performance concern and gives a 3.5-million-patron example; no priority marker or broader agreement is recorded.
requirements.description: The system shall generate the inactive-patrons report for a dataset containing 3.5 million patron records within 30 minutes when run under the acceptance-test environment and workload. During that run, interactive circulation and OPAC requests shall continue to meet the response-time target for online-hours workload continuity. Acceptance testing shall verify the report results against a reference data set.

requirements.name: Large-Scale Batch Updates
requirements.priority_rationale: The need is based on a concrete 9.6-million-item collection and technical staff concern, but is supported by one source and has no explicit high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The system shall process large batch updates in smaller chunks to limit database locking. It shall scale to batch transfer operations in collections containing millions of items without excessive locking or performance degradation. The stated environment includes 9.6 million items.

requirements.name: Management Scope Boundary
requirements.priority_rationale: The boundary was agreed in meeting minutes, but it is a project-scope constraint rather than a blocker to system operation.
requirements.description: The project shall specify requirements that directly or indirectly relate to management activities. It shall not attempt to fully specify unrelated ILS modules. This boundary shall keep the specification focused on the agreed management scope.

requirements.name: Process Flow Documentation
requirements.priority_rationale: Process documentation is requested in two sources and is useful to staff and developers, but it has no high-priority marker.
requirements.description: The software developer shall provide a thorough high-level description of major processes. The documentation shall cover bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports. This documentation shall help staff and developers understand how data and processes flow through the system.

requirements.name: Report Output Accuracy
requirements.priority_rationale: A single draft source states the quality need without a priority marker or measurable acceptance criteria.
requirements.description: The system shall produce report outputs that match the selected report criteria and source data. For each release, acceptance testing shall run a defined suite of reports against reference data containing known records, totals, and edge cases; all returned records and aggregate values shall match the expected results. The system shall identify execution failures and shall not present a partial result as a complete report.

requirements.name: SRS Audience And Readability
requirements.priority_rationale: One meeting source identifies both audiences and the readability need; no higher-priority marker is given.
requirements.description: The Software Requirements Specification shall serve library managers and staff who may contribute requirements, as well as software project managers and developers. It shall be readable to non-technical readers while remaining specific enough for developers. This balance shall support both stakeholder review and implementation.

requirements.name: Transactional Batch Updates
requirements.priority_rationale: One source requests transaction safety for batch updates, with no explicit priority marker or additional agreement.
requirements.description: The system shall perform batch location updates within database transactions. Each batch shall preserve data safety and consistency if an update does not complete successfully. This shall reduce the risk of partially applied location changes.

discarded.reason: These candidates require interfaces with vendor websites and ingestion of standard-format data files, which are integration capabilities rather than query-building, filtering, or candidate-selection behavior.

discarded.name: Circulate Reference Draft

discarded.name: Defer UI Specification
discarded.reason: This describes when the project should produce UI specifications rather than system behavior.

discarded.name: Reports Specification Project Task
discarded.reason: This is a project documentation deliverable about a future release rather than a requirement for the system.

discarded.name: Iterative Prototype Methodology

discarded.name: Member Interview Assignment

discarded.name: Follow-Up Meeting Schedule

discarded.name: Architectural Subcommittee Meeting

discarded.name: Foundation Draft Selection

discarded.name: Reports Mission Statement
